want.who_she_is: Iris Marlow, 31. Her aunt Perrine died in March and left her the Marlow Baths in Hollis Springs along with the note on the building: $61,000, eleven months. She quit a job she cannot get back, sold her car for the roof, and sleeps in the attic flat over the changing room. What she has to lose is not the building — it is Perrine's name. The Marlow was the respectable house, the one families came to, and that respectability is the collateral every transgression is paid out of.
want.appetite: To be necessary to people at the moment they have nothing on — and every time someone becomes a regular, the wanting resets one notch further in. Release 41 adds a new name on the night list, a new room upstairs, a new line on Del's service board.
want.ascent: At the bottom she works the front desk in a robe, hands out towels and tea to four daylight regulars, and three rooms are open. At the top she runs a members' night in a building where every floor is unlocked, and she is the one on the tiles. Three tiers plus a counterweight: STEAM (what she is seen in and who is in the room: robe -> shift -> wrap -> nothing; women's hours -> mixed -> after close), SERVICE (what her hands do: towel and tea -> scrub -> oil -> the private-room list), HOUSE (which rooms are hers to use: cold plunge -> boiler floor -> the upstairs privates -> Perrine's old members' floor, bought with repair money), and PROPRIETY, the counterweight — Perrine's clean name, spent to climb the other three, and what buys the daylight trade and the inspector's blind eye.
want.charge: transformation (primary) + reversal (secondary) — she came to save an inheritance and becomes the thing people come for, while everyone holding power over her (the note, the permit, the heat) ends up asking her for something

why_this_person.npc_del: Perrine's attendant, 50s, stayed on unpaid, knows every valve and every regular's habit. She withholds approval, and Iris wants to be told she is doing it right by the only person qualified to say so.
why_this_person.npc_ivo: Runs the boiler and the spring line — the one man who can turn the heat off. Basement, quiet hours, sees her at her worst. He never asks, and he could take.
why_this_person.npc_warren: Town clerk, holds the occupancy grade. Wants her and cannot be seen wanting her. The charge is being wanted by the man whose whole job is respectability.
why_this_person.npc_june: 68, forty years of Tuesdays, the town's permission in one body. Frank about bodies in a way that gives Iris room to be.
why_this_person.npc_casper: The cousin who expected the building, lives four streets over, still calls it his. He watched her grow up and now has to ask her for things.
why_this_person.npc_nell: 23, took the back room for the season, swims at 2 a.m. The only person in Hollis who never met Perrine — the one Iris can be new in front of.

crude_ceiling._notes: Written as the actual permitted words, per the-want.md §6 — a ceiling described abstractly gets written around. June's is a SPEECH ceiling: she says all three about other people and her own authored acts stop at hands. Warren's words are permitted only behind a shut door; in daylight he says 'Miss Marlow' and nothing else, and that gap is his charge. Ivo's list is permitted but he speaks about six lines in the whole ladder — his register is that the prose does the body and he does not narrate himself.

want.register_home: The crude register lives on the repeatable surfaces — the scrub room floor, the plunge, the private rooms — re-entered every in-game day. Nothing crude is saved for a one-time capstone.
want.deletion_test: Cut Del and the game loses its standard: nobody's approval means anything after that.

board.ceiling_note: Top band is left UNBOUNDED at v0.1 (min = 55, no max), which promises nothing beyond the rung it names. Gate 8 judges the top band's MIN, so v0.1 must author a 55 gate on each tier. Each release raises the wall by adding a band and the content behind it — the honest-wall rule from the-release.md.

decisions.note: THE NOTE IS WEEKLY, NOT MONTHLY, and this was forced by the engine, not chosen: rent_due_day is validated against weekday names only (template_import.py:4786, VALID_DAYS) and there is no monthly period. So the design's '$540 on the 1st' became $135 every Friday, drawn in person by Casper at the desk. Cost: none to the fiction — a private family note drawn weekly out of the till is if anything more in character for Casper's father — and the pressure now lands four times as often, which matches the reference game's weekly rent.

Pass A shipped the frame: 0_systems_spec (meters, bands, the note, 24 quest cards), 1_metadata_and_locations (8 locations, 6 NPCs with 13 schedule rows, the wardrobe), 2_one_shots (the opening chain plus the first explicit beat). Builds green. Gates 7/15 pass — guidance and the no-silent-retirement rule are green from the frame alone. Gate 12 caught a real defect: the ledger said the_back_room while the TOML shipped the_lodgers_room (renamed for the-voice.md R1 — a nav label must say who is through the door). Ledger corrected. The dialogue-attribution lint on canvas_opening is a FALSE POSITIVE: verified in the built HTML, an explicit npcId renders 'Del:' correctly.

Board approved in chat and recorded; phase advanced want -> board. The economy is where the design earns its keep: the note is privately held by Casper, so the monthly obligation has a face who is also a cast member with a grievance. Cost: he can never be a purely optional character, and if he is ever cut the obligation loses its face and R3 breaks.

Want written and approved in chat before any file was created. Four tiers declared here rather than at board time because the ascent is stated as access and the tiers ARE the access: STEAM, SERVICE, HOUSE, plus the PROPRIETY counterweight. crude_ceiling is deliberately left empty — it is owed at the board phase, written as actual permitted words per character per tier, never described abstractly.

FILL WAS THE WHOLE COST. 17/18 gates were green at ~18k words and the last one took the game from 18k to 36,019 — mean 4,502 against a 4,500 floor. Nothing about the world changed in that stretch; the rooms got written. Final distribution: pool 10,413 (29%, anchor), desk 4,614, scrub 4,345, boiler 4,167, changing 3,565, attic 3,316, street 2,950, lodger's 2,649.

THE PIVOT, CAUGHT BY MEASUREMENT, TWICE. First scoring of the explicit surfaces: 7 of 60 beats carried 3+ frozen-list words; the rest named a body part and left the body inside the same beat. Rewritten against the per-beat score, not by eye: 34 of 60, and the whole-game ratio went 8.0% -> 41%. It regressed a second time near the end (7.4%, under the floor) because ~15k words of world/economy prose diluted it — fixed by putting the last 2,000 words into repeatable explicit surfaces rather than by trimming anything.

UNREACHABLE-CANVAS BUG, MINE, TWICE. Writing rungs first and wiring the hub choices second left six canvases with no referrer: they resolved to '(unplaced)', counted for nothing, and would have been unreachable in play. The tell was word count flat while sentence count rose. Every rung after that was written with its hub choice in the same pass.

LINTS REVIEWED, NOT SUPPRESSED. Dialogue attribution flagged 11 canvases; verified in the BUILT HTML (double-unescaped, since cascade beats carry entity-encoded markup) that all five spot-checked lines render the right name — false positive class, an explicit npcId is enough. One was a real defect and was fixed: June was speaking on Spring Street where she has no schedule row; converted to reported speech. Map lint: 'yard', 'hall', 'front door', 'stairs', 'basement' are all deliberate — off-map workplaces, the chapel, the street frontage, the locked members' stairs, and the_boiler respectively. 'corridor' was the only fair hit and now has a surface of its own at the pool.

phase advanced board -> release. From here the unit of work is a release: events at existing places with existing characters, zero new locations by default, and the Want re-read every cycle (last_read_at_release now 0.1).

LIVE PLAY-TEST, headless Chromium against the built HTML — the checks gates.py structurally cannot make. (1) MONEY IS NOT CLAMPED, verified by effect diff: a real door shift ran 95 -> 135, while the clamped path in the same page caps at 100 (85,100,100,100,100). This is engine.md §21, the defect that made a shipped game unwinnable with every gate green; Steam is clean. (2) Age gate -> opening funnel -> free roam works: doors_open sets and the player lands at the_front_desk. (3) Schedule grid exact: 13/13 declared windows put the right character in the right room and 3/3 negative controls stay empty (June absent Monday, Warren absent Wednesday, Ivo absent at 14:00 — his row starts at 20:00). (4) Locked doors render as span.locked-choice. (5) Guidance resolves at BOTH ends: at zero state 3 story cards + 6 npc cards, each naming a place and a verb; at maxed meters all nine retire to end-of-content/terminal cards and nothing renders blank. (6) No uncaught JS errors.

HARNESS FACTS, all found the hard way and worth knowing before the next play-test: SugarCube's State/Engine are NOT bare globals in this build — they hang off window.SugarCube. time_state.current_day is a day NAME string ('Monday'), while current_hour/current_minute are ints; writing ints into current_day silently kills every weekday match. setup.pickQuestsCards accepts exactly one scope, the literal 'story_goals', and returns [] for anything else — which reads identically to an empty guidance page and is how a false alarm gets raised. Presence is setup.getNpcsPresentAtLocation(slug); setup.getNpcLocation returns a location UUID, not a slug. Playwright text selectors break on the rendered labels (✓, curly apostrophes) — click by substring inside page.evaluate instead.
